summary: This script checks if a dev container welcome message has already been added to a user's bash configuration file, and if not, it appends a block of aliases and welcome text. This prevents the welcome message from appearing multiple times if the script runs again.

explanations.2: This line makes the script stop immediately if any command fails, if any undefined variable is used, or if a piped command fails — it's a safety net to catch mistakes early.
explanations.4: This constructs the path to the user's bashrc file, using the OS_USERNAME variable if it's set, otherwise defaulting to 'node' as the username.
explanations.7: The grep command searches for the exact marker line in the bashrc file; the -q flag means 'quiet' (no output), and -xF means match the whole line exactly as literal text. The ! negates it, so this checks 'if the marker is NOT already there'.
explanations.8: The cat command with <<EOF reads all the text between this line and the closing EOF, then appends it (>>) to the bashrc file.
explanations.11: This sets a variable called BLOG_HOST_DIR in bashrc, using its current value if it exists, or an empty string if it doesn't — the curly braces let you provide a fallback default.
